newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Two Indonesians jailed for election riot.
newsitem.headline: Two Indonesians jailed for election riot.

text.p: An Indonesian court has jailed two men for looting and carrying weapons during a pre-election riot last May in which 123 people died, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

The report said Judge B.F. Siregar of the district court in the South Kalimantan provincial capital of Banjarmasin sentenced Rade'i bin Mutasi to nine months jail and Ratiman (Eds: one word) to two and a half months jail after the riot on May 23.
Rade'i was found guilty of carrying illegal weapons, while Ratiman was convicted of looting. The prosecution had asked for two years jail for Rade'i and five months for Ratiman.

Three others were sentenced last week to between nine and 24 months for carrying knives during the riot, which started after clashes between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
The rioting was followed by looting in which a number of buildings, including shopping centres, hotels, banks, churches and government offices and more than 100 vehicles were burned.
Twenty-five people, including the five already convicted, stand accused of either taking part in the riots, looting or carrying illegal weapons.
They were among the more than 100 people detained after the riot on the last day of Indonesia's violence-stained election campaign. Golkar easily won the election on May 29.

Officials said most of the 123 dead were burned to death in the city's Mitra Plaza shopping mall after it was set ablaze, but most of the bodies could not be identified and were buried anonymously in a mass grave.
